newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-LARA ISSUES CHALLENGE TO BATSMEN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LARA ISSUES CHALLENGE TO BATSMEN.

text.p: Vice-captain Brian Lara has called for support from his fellow West Indian batsmen on the eve of his side's five-test series against Australia.
Lara, holder of the world records for the highest test and first-class scores, said on Thursday the West Indian top order must share the responsibility of winning back the Frank Worrell trophy.
"It will be the greatest challenge for us. We want to get back to the days when we were scoring 400-plus every innings," Lara told reporters at the Gabba.
"Lately the bowlers have been winning us matches but the batting has not been doing us justice.
"We were known in the late 1970s and 1980s as having four fast bowlers. A lot of people said these were the guys who won us test matches.
"But they forgot that Viv Richards, Desmond Haynes, Clive Lloyd, Richie Richardson, Larry Gomes and others won us test matches with their batting."
Australia beat West Indies 2-1 in the Caribbean in May last year, ending the hosts' 15-year unbeaten run.
"Now we have the chance to regain that glory and reinstate ourselves as the best cricket team in the world," Lara said.
The tourists are expected to announce their line-up before the start of play on Friday.
Australia captain Mark Taylor said Ricky Ponting was ready to take on the responsibility of batting at number three after the retirement last year of the long-serving David Boon.
"Whether you are three, four or five against the West Indies you are going to get the same sort of bowling," he said.
"The only thing is you might go in at 0-1 or 201-1."
Australia's bowling attack has been strengthened by the recall from injury of leg-spinner Shane Warne and the availability of fast bowler Glenn McGrath.
Warne missed the defeat in last month's one-off test against India after failing to recover in time from the effects of surgery on the ring finger of his bowling hand in May.
McGrath, Australia's main new ball strike bowler, passed a fitness test on a blistered heel on Wednesday.
Inexperienced pair Jason Gillespie and Michael Kasprowicz are expected to fight it out for the remaining available place in the bowling line-up alongside McGrath and Paul Reiffel.

Australia (from) - Mark Taylor (captain), Matthew Elliott, Ricky Ponting, Mark Waugh, Steve Waugh, Michael Bevan, Ian Healy, Shane Warne, Paul Reiffel, Glenn McGrath, Michael Kasprowicz, Jason Gillespie.

West Indies (from) - Robert Samuels, Adrian Griffith, Brian Lara, Shivnarine Chanderpaul, Carl Hooper, Jimmy Adams, Roland Holder, Courtney Brown, Kenneth Benjamin, Curtly Ambrose, Courtney Walsh (captain), Nixon McLean, Patterson Thompson.
